correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the convention: perfect-matching complex faces are edge matchings extendible to perfect matchings, not the ordinary matching complex. The one-step edge rotation has only perimeter orbit size 2n and rung orbit size n, so exactly empty and all-rung invariant faces; signed reduced Lefschetz number 0. Two-step rotation splits rung edges into two orbits of size n/2 and rim edges into two alternating perfect-matchings of size n; exactly six invariant faces yield reduced Lefschetz 2. The general fixed-face sign (-1)^(number_of_edge_orbits+1) includes the augmented empty face. Theorem 21 of Agarwal–Basak (full primary v2 inspected) gives H_d=Q² and no other reduced homology. Thus tr(T)=0,tr(T²)=2(-1)^d. T is finite order and hence complex diagonalizable; two unit-modulus eigenvalues whose sum is ±2 coincide at ±1, giving the operator identity and parity orders. Independently enumerated edge orbits/fixed faces for n=4,6,8; these are finite checks, not the n-uniform homotopy theorem.
residual_risks: Relies on the published non-equivariant Theorem 21 for all n; direct code checks only finite n and mod-two Betti numbers.
No integral lattice representation or odd-n classification is asserted.

value.rationale: Determines the full rational cyclic action of the generator, not merely a sphere count or involution character. The unexpected collapse of a geometric 2n-order rotation to homological order two or four is an invariant a researcher studying equivariant graph topology can use directly. It is a uniform infinite-family representation refinement with a short exact Lefschetz proof; it is neither a renaming of the homotopy theorem nor an arbitrary tiny example.
residual_risks: Only rational generator action is determined, not integral representation or complete automorphism group.

final_claim: For even n>=4, one-step vertex rotation on the rational degree n/2-1 reduced homology of the Möbius-ladder perfect-matching complex has trace zero and T²=(-1)^(n/2-1) I. Its induced cyclic operator has precise order 2 when n=2 mod 4 and order 4 when n=0 mod 4.
limitations: Inherited all-parameter homotopy classification is not independently re-proved. Finite orbit checks corroborate, not establish, the universal formula.
